findings.highlight: Shirou, who has fallen into a pit just by getting sidetracked
findings.evidenceJa: このままじゃ現世復帰が無理めな士郎
findings.governingReading: Shirou, for whom returning to the present world looks difficult at this rate
findings.explanation: The English removes the mock-afterlife premise that the rescue corner must restore dead Shirou to this world.

findings.highlight: fallen into a pit just by getting sidetracked
findings.evidenceJa: わき道から谷底へまっしぐら
findings.governingReading: went straight from a slight side path to the bottom of the valley
findings.explanation: Pit replaces the escalating route metaphor of a tiny deviation leading directly to the valley bottom.

findings.highlight: if the fault isn’t all hers
findings.governingReading: if responsibility is divided half and half
findings.explanation: Not all hers removes the exact equal division between Shirou and Saber that licenses Saber’s absence from the dojo.
Real introduces a hierarchy of authenticity; the dojo warns that poor choices prevent reaching the correct route ending.

findings.highlight: Get your act together and win.
findings.evidenceJa: 勝って兜の緒を締めよ
findings.governingReading: After winning, tighten the cords of your helmet: remain vigilant even in victory.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the proverb into preparation before winning and erases its warning against relaxing after success.

findings.highlight: We’ll be waiting in the next Tiger Dojo!
findings.evidenceJa: 次のタイガー道場で待ってるよ
findings.governingReading: I will be waiting for you at the next Tiger Dojo.
findings.explanation: The English changes Taiga’s singular promise into an unmarked plural and weakens the host’s direct persona.
